Because solute amount is conserved: $$ C1 V1 = C2 V2 $$ Where: input: C1 input: V1 input: C2 input: V2 Using the concentration relation from the previous lesson: $$ n1 = C1 V1 $$ $$ n2 = C2 V2 $$ input: C1 input: V1 input: C2 input: V2; Concentration Definitions: Concentration Definitions: pH from hydrogen ion concentration. Chemistry uses this family in the pH definition. The reusable formula is: $$ \mathrm{pH} = -\log{10}[H^+] $$ input: [H^+] output: pH Chemistry uses this family in molarity. The reusable formula is: $$ C = \frac{n}{V} $$ input: n input: V output: C; The Dilution Law C 1 V 1 C 2 V 2: The Dilution Law C 1 V 1 C 2 V 2: Conservation Of Carried Substance. If the amount of solute stays the same before and after dilution, the reusable family is conservation of carried substance. The reusable formula is: $$ n1 = n2 $$ input: n1 output: n2 Using the concentration relation from the previous lesson: $$ n1 = C1 V1 $$ $$ n2 = C2 V2 $$ input: C1 input: V1 input: C2 input: V2
